Cite class downgraded to TIER-1-NAMED-AUTHOR-QUOTE-PROVISIONAL with REQUIRED metadata: (a) ISBN/DOI + page + verbatim-quote inline; (b) verifier-identity disclosure (who-verified-when, e.g., `[VERIFIED 2026-05-04 by orchestrator against book Tip #15 verbatim text]`); (c) explicit `non-automatable: true` marker so review hooks know to defer to human sign-off; (d) **HARD-GATE ELIGIBILITY TEST** *(Round-3 amendment a per T3 R3 NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.82 same-class finding on commit `1b87a6e`; supersedes round-2 "MUST prefer" soft preference framing — preference is not gateable; eligibility is)*: PROVISIONAL admission is admissible ONLY when DOI landing page + accessible PDF / publisher excerpt / archived scan (license-permitting) was SEARCHED AND UNAVAILABLE. The commit body MUST document the search (which DOI/publisher/archive was queried + return shape — e.g., "searched ACM DOI 10.1145/<doi> 2026-05-05 — paywall-only, no excerpt found; searched Internet Archive — no scan; searched publisher excerpt page — none"). Mere preference is INSUFFICIENT — if any auditable surrogate exists (DOI/PDF/excerpt/scan), use it as the normative source instead of the physical-only book cite. e.g., ACM DOI `https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/<doi>` for ACM papers IS auditable when paywall-free. Secondary aggregator URLs (Wikipedia, `https://pragprog.com/tips/`, `https://martinfowler.com/bliki/<topic>.html`, `c2.com/cgi/wiki`) are VERIFICATION PROXIES only — they help re-verify the primary quote without owning the book physically, but are NOT cited as normative source. **Independent named-reviewer sign-off mandate** *(Round-3 amendment b per T3 R3 NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.82 same-class finding on commit `1b87a6e`; supersedes round-2 "Lower-confidence reviewer-sign-off mandate" sole-orchestrator framing — sole-orchestrator verification is no longer admissible)*: rule edits citing TIER-1-NAMED-AUTHOR-QUOTE-PROVISIONAL MUST cite a SECOND verifier-identity BEYOND the orchestrator who replayed the verbatim quote against the source — commit body MUST embed BOTH verifier-identity-1 (the orchestrator, e.g., `[VERIFIED 2026-05-05 by orchestrator against book Tip #15 verbatim text]`) AND verifier-identity-2 (the independent named reviewer, e.g., `[VERIFIED 2026-05-05 by <human-name> against same book + same page + same quote]`) with explicit `[VERIFIED yyyy-mm-dd by <name> against <source>]` markers for each. .claude\rules\deprecation-discipline.md:40:3. **Does a replacement exist?** → If no, build the replacement FIRST. Never deprecate without an alternative. **Replacement readiness gate** (per Wave 82x codex T1 fix-forward F-003 / upstream SKILL.md:71-75): replacement must (a) cover critical use cases of the old system, (b) have documentation + migration guides, AND (c) be proven in production (not just "theoretically better") before deprecation starts.
.claude\rules\deprecation-discipline.md:51:**Default to advisory.** Use compulsory only when maintenance cost or risk justifies forcing migration. Compulsory deprecation requires migration tooling, documentation, and support; a deadline alone is not sufficient. Per Wave 82x codex T1 fix-forward F-002: upstream Osmani SKILL.md:62-65 mandates default-to-advisory + compulsory-with-tooling guardrail.
.claude\rules\deprecation-discipline.md:58:4. **Removal**: delete old code, dependencies, docs, references — verify ZERO active usage via metrics/logs/dependency analysis (NOT just `rg "<old-symbol>"` text search; per Wave 82x codex T1 fix-forward F-005 / upstream SKILL.md:112-118,201-206); then remove tests + docs + config + deprecation notices
.claude\rules\deprecation-discipline.md:62:**If you own the surface being deprecated, you own user migration or backward-compatible updates; do not leave consumers to discover the path themselves.** Per Wave 82x codex T1 fix-forward F-004 / upstream SKILL.md:106. This makes the owner responsibility EXPLICIT — distinct from the "Announce-and-leave" anti-pattern below (which describes the failure mode this rule prevents).

Go to [Settings > Capabilities](https://claude.ai/settings/capabilities)\n2. Enable Skills toggle\n3. docs\sota-architecture-audit\future-evolution\_extension-and-reaudit-metadata.json:475:    "readme_head_2000": "# Superpowers\n\nSuperpowers is a complete software development methodology for your coding agents, built on top of a set of composable skills and some initial instructions that make sure your agent uses them.\n\n## Quickstart\n\nGive your agent Superpowers: [Claude Code](#claude-code), [Codex CLI](#codex-cli), [Codex App](#codex-app), [Factory Droid](#factory-droid), [Gemini CLI](#gemini-cli), [OpenCode](#opencode), [Cursor](#cursor), [GitHub Copilot CLI](#github-copilot-cli).\n\n## How it works\n\nIt starts from the moment you fire up your coding agent. As soon as it sees that you're building something, it *doesn't* just jump into trying to write code. Instead, it steps back and asks you what you're really trying to do. \n\nOnce it's teased a spec out of the conversation, it shows it to you in chunks short enough to actually read and digest. \n\nAfter you've signed off on the design, your agent puts together an implementation plan that's clear enough for an enthusiastic junior engineer with poor taste, no judgement, no project context, and an aversion to testing to follow. It emphasizes true red/green TDD, YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It), and DRY. \n\nNext up, once you say \"go\", it launches a *subagent-driven-development* process, having agents work through each engineering task, inspecting and reviewing their work, and continuing forward. It's not uncommon for Claude to be able to work autonomously for a couple hours at a time without deviating from the plan you put together.\n\nThere's a bunch more to it, but that's the core of the system. And because the skills trigger automatically, you don't need to do anything special. Your coding agent just has Superpowers.\n\n\n## Sponsorship\n\nIf Superpowers has helped you do stuff that makes money and you are so inclined, I'd greatly appreciate it if you'd consider [sponsoring my opensource work](https://github.com/sponsors/obra).\n\nThanks! \n\n- Jesse\n\n\n## Installation\n\nInstallation differs by harness. 275:### The 4-skill stack — meta-skills active in this runtime
276:
277:This runtime runs with 4 meta-skills active that govern multi-skill orchestration. They auto-fire per their `description:` triggers — no manual invocation required for the meta-layer to activate. Skill discovery is Anthropic CC native mechanism (per `https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills`) — Claude reads `description:` frontmatter of every available SKILL.md and invokes via the `Skill` tool when description matches the current task.
278:
279:| # | Meta-skill | Source plugin | Role |
280:|---|---|---|---|
281:| 1 | `using-superpowers` | superpowers@claude-plugins-official | "1% rule" — invoke any skill that has even a 1% chance of applying. Defines Skill Priority (Process skills first / Implementation skills second). Red Flags table catches rationalizations. |
282:| 2 | `using-agent-skills` | agent-skills@addy-agent-skills | Discovery + invocation governance for the 21 addy engineering-phase skills. Auto-fires at session start to surface relevant skill for current task. |
283:| 3 | `skill-comply` | everything-claude-code | Post-invocation verification that skill use was correct + complete (verifies skill checklist completion if skill body had one). |
284:| 4 | `skill-creator` | skill-creator@claude-plugins-official | Authoring loop: draft → eval → iterate → benchmark → optimize description for triggering accuracy. Use when creating new skills OR when an existing skill should be improved. |
285:
286:### How and when to invoke skills (mandatory discipline)
287:
288:**For Claude (main thread)**:
289:- Per `using-superpowers` 1% rule: invoke ANY relevant skill BEFORE response or action. Skill check comes BEFORE clarifying questions / file exploration / planning.
290:- Multiple skills: Process skills (brainstorming / debugging / verification-before-completion) determine HOW; Implementation skills (frontend-design / api-and-interface-design / TDD) guide EXECUTION. Layer them when both apply.
291:- Announce: "Using [skill] to [purpose]" before each invocation per `using-superpowers` skill flow digraph.
292:- Follow skill EXACTLY when rigid (TDD / debugging); adapt principles when flexible (patterns).
293:
294:**For subagents** (per CCBP `claude-subagents.md:32-34` `skills:` preload field):
295:- Subagent briefs MUST include skill-awareness clause when role demands. Standing directive `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/advanced-agent-team-standing-directive.md` invariant applies — agent briefs cite TIER-1 sources at file:line + HEAD SHA, including relevant SKILL.md files for the agent's role.
296:- Subagent frontmatter `skills:` field can preload specific skills (CC 2.1+); `allowed-tools` controls tool surface; `context: fork` runs in isolated subagent context per CCBP 15-field spec.
297:- Common preload pairings:
298:  - `sota-researcher` agent → preload `deep-research` + `research-ops` ECC skills + `iterative-retrieval` + `using-agent-skills` (auto-fires regardless via discovery)

301:  - `debugger` agent → preload `systematic-debugging` (superpowers) + `debugging-and-error-recovery` (addy) + `agent-introspection-debugging` (ECC)
302:  - `verifier` agent → preload `verification-before-completion` (superpowers) + `eval-harness` (ECC)
303:
304:**For multi-skill orchestration** (chained or layered):
305:- **Chain example**: brainstorming → writing-plans → subagent-driven-development → test-driven-development → requesting-code-review → finishing-a-development-branch (per superpowers workflow grammar L7 sequence)
306:- **Layer example**: while implementing a feature: `feature-dev` (claude-plugins-official) PLUS `incremental-implementation` (addy) PLUS `tdd` (superpowers) PLUS `safety-guard` (ECC) PLUS `verification-before-completion` (superpowers)
307:- **Anti-pattern**: invoking ONLY one skill when 2-4 apply. The 1% rule is bidirectional — even if uncertain whether skill X applies, invoke it; if it turns out wrong, drop it.
